tagline.text: See crocodiles, tigers and orangutans up close at a Davao zoo

location.label: Location
location.text: Riverfront Corporate City, Diversion Road, Barangay Ma-a, Davao City

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~1,500 (per person for a half day, covering admission, Grab and a meal)

children.text: Davao Crocodile Park is a crocodile farm and zoo in the Ma-a district of Davao City. You can see saltwater and freshwater crocodiles as well as tigers, orangutans, birds of prey and parrots at close range, and keeper talks and feeding times make it a good stop with children. It is about 20–30 minutes from downtown by car, so it fits easily into a Davao itinerary as a half-day outing.

Davao Crocodile Park is a zoo and crocodile park on Diversion Road in the Ma-a district, southwest of Davao City. It is a family-friendly attraction that many visitors to Mindanao's largest city stop by at least once, and its address is given as inside Riverfront Corporate City. Ma-a is about 20–30 minutes by car from the city center, so it is an easy half-day trip from the airport or a downtown hotel.

Crocodiles are what made the park famous. Saltwater and freshwater crocodiles are kept in pens grouped by size, and there are enclosures and a viewing deck where you can see everything from hatchlings to large adults. The park's symbol, a saltwater crocodile named Pangil, measured about 18 feet (about 5.5m) and died of cancer complications on January 25, 2025. You can no longer see Pangil alive, but the park has said it keeps his story on display and is preparing a new attraction. Older reviews that promise "the biggest crocodile" are now out of date, so keep that in mind.

Besides crocodiles, the park has big cats such as Siberian tigers, an orangutan, raptors, parrots and other birds, snakes and lizards, and Philippine warty pigs. According to one visitor account, the park has around 61 animals and about 90 percent of them are rescues that cannot be returned to the wild. It is not a very large zoo, but the keeper talks, where staff introduce the animals themselves, and the feeding times make even a short visit worthwhile.

The same complex also has a butterfly garden (the Butterfly House) and the Tribu K'Mindanawan cultural village, which introduces Indigenous Philippine culture, and some reports say admission can include them. What the ticket covers changes from year to year, so check at the ticket booth. A common plan is to put this park on a Davao city tour and pair nature spots such as Eden Nature Park or the Philippine Eagle Center on another day. For first-timers, a natural route is to buy your ticket, fill in the visitor registration slip, and start at the crocodile pens before moving on to the tigers and orangutan, then the birds of prey and bird area. Count on about
1 hour
for the crocodile area alone, about
1.5–2 hours
for a standard visit, and
3–4 hours
if you add a show and lunch. If you have children, plan around the keeper talks and feeding times for the best experience.

A viewing deck looks down on pens where saltwater and freshwater crocodiles are separated by size. You can compare hatchlings and large adults at a glance. From the deck above the pens you can watch the crocodiles move in the water, so linger for a while.

blocks.title: The story of Pangil and the memorial display

children.text: Pangil, the 18-foot saltwater crocodile, died on January 25, 2025. You can no longer see him alive, but the park continues to tell his story through displays, so ask the staff what is on show.
You can see Siberian tigers and a rescued orangutan. Feeding sessions for animals such as tigers and ostriches are reported to run in the afternoon, so check the schedule in advance.
Keepers explain the animals' habits and the stories of how they were rescued. One visitor account says the sessions take place around
and
, but times can vary from day to day.

Raptors such as white-bellied sea eagles and brahminy kites perch on stands, and parrots and lories greet visitors. The bird noise is loud, and it is an area children especially enjoy. Some reviews say the birds even mimic human speech.
You can see butterflies flying freely in the butterfly garden in the same complex. Whether it is included in your ticket can change by visit, so check.
A cultural village introducing Indigenous Mindanao culture is next door. Evening performances are said to be held on some nights, so call ahead if you plan to arrive late.

The restaurant in the complex is known for crocodile tasting dishes, and the gift shop near the exit sells crocodile leather goods. Crocodile leather and teeth may be restricted from import in some countries, so check the rules before you buy.

items.title: Half-day plan
items.subtitle: Animals in the morning, then lunch

children.text: Leave your downtown Davao hotel by Grab. The ride takes about
20–30 minutes
from the city center.
Enter as soon as the park opens, fill in the visitor registration slip at the ticket booth and buy your ticket. It is best to see the outdoor animals before it gets hot.
Walk through the crocodile pens and viewing deck, the tiger and orangutan area, and the birds of prey and parrot area in turn.
If a keeper talk is scheduled, catch it at the right time. Check the schedule at the entrance.
See the Butterfly House and the cultural village, then have lunch at the restaurant in the complex.
Take a Grab or taxi back to downtown Davao and continue with the rest of your plans.

items.title: Full Davao day
items.subtitle: Combining the park with a city tour

children.text: Have breakfast at your hotel and call a Grab.
Arrive at the park and look around the crocodile, tiger and bird areas.
Catch a keeper talk or the butterfly garden, then have lunch in the complex.
Go back downtown and rest at your hotel for a while, avoiding the midday heat.
Visit San Pedro Cathedral and the downtown malls.
Have dinner at a downtown seafood restaurant or durian stand.
If you plan to visit the park in the afternoon, time it for the feeding session but be sure to check the closing time.
Nonstop flights from Manila (NAIA) to Francisco Bangoy International Airport, Davao (DVO) take about
2 hours 10 minutes
and are operated by airlines such as Philippine Airlines, Cebu Pacific and AirAsia. Check the airlines' announcements for routes and schedules.
There are many flights from Manila, so it is easy to plan your trip.

items.title: From the airport to the park

children.text: A Grab or taxi from the airport takes about
15–20 minutes
(it varies with traffic).
By public transport, you can take a jeepney toward Ma-a from downtown and get off at the park entrance, but it requires a transfer and takes about
30–40 minutes
From the city center it takes about
20–30 minutes
by Grab.
There is free parking at the park entrance, which makes a rental car convenient too.
If you take a taxi, ask the driver to use the meter. A Grab is easier because you know the price in advance.
A Grab back may be hard to book, so it can help to get the driver's contact number on the way in.
Davao lies relatively outside the typhoon belt, so it is a good place to visit year-round. Since most of the sights are outdoors, the key is to choose times with less rain and less heat.

During the day, the morning when the park opens and the late afternoon when the sun is lower are the most comfortable for walking and also overlap with feeding times. Many reviews say weekdays are quieter than weekends.

Showers in the rainy season often pass quickly, but the pens and the viewing deck are outdoors and the ground can get slippery when it rains. If rain is forecast, visit in the morning and switch to an indoor mall or café in the afternoon.

Most people stay in downtown Davao rather than near the park. A mid-range hotel in the city center puts you close to malls, restaurants and the cathedral, and the park is an easy Grab ride away.
The park has a riverside restaurant that is known to serve crocodile tasting dishes. Many visitors return downtown and have dinner at a Davao durian, seafood or barbecue restaurant.

The complex is also said to sell ice cream made with crocodile eggs, so try it if you are curious. Menus and prices change, so check the on-site notices. Many hotels do not allow durian in the rooms, so check your hotel's rules first.
Admission and opening hours differ by source, so confirm with the park's Facebook page or by phone before you go. The phone number reported for the park is
The ticket booth asks you to fill in a visitor registration slip. One slip is enough for a group.
If you go early in the morning, it is cooler and the animals are more active.
Bring sunscreen, a hat, water and comfortable shoes, and carry a little cash.
Check the feeding and keeper-talk times at the entrance and plan around them.
To combine the park with city sightseeing, put it in half a day of a Davao city tour and save the rest for another day.
The "biggest crocodile Pangil" mentioned in older reviews can no longer be seen, so set your expectations accordingly.
When taking photos, keep your distance from the animals and do not use flash. Birds and raptors can be startled.
Some reviews say the park is not very large. Lower your expectations and make use of the keeper talks to get more out of the visit.
Public transport in Davao is inconvenient, so many travelers use both Grab and taxis. Buying a SIM card at the airport in advance makes it easier to book rides.
Lifting a child over the railing or putting your hand inside a cage is prohibited and extremely dangerous.
Do not feed the animals on your own or throw objects at them. Feeding is allowed only when staff permit it.
Hold children's hands so they do not climb on the railings.
Notices say that bringing pets, smoking, and entering while under the influence of alcohol or drugs may be restricted.
The park tends to close in the late afternoon, so you may not be admitted if you arrive late.
There are import rules for souvenirs such as crocodile leather and teeth when taking them to Korea or other countries, so check them first.
This is a place where rescued animals are kept, so avoid provoking them or shouting, and follow staff instructions.
A big city about
20–30 minutes
by car from the park, with malls, durian stands and seafood restaurants.
A resort garden in the highlands outside Davao, good for walks in cool weather. It is best to set aside a separate day.
A conservation center for the endangered Philippine eagle, which pairs well with a nature and wildlife itinerary.
A church in the city center that is easy to add to a city sightseeing plan.
An island off Davao with beaches and resorts, reachable as a day trip or an overnight stay.
